Martellus draws southern Africa from reports of Dias. Florentine geographers know the Mediterranean well. Maps still greatly exaggerate Asia's eastward extent. Local: Henricus Martellus (maps showing Dias's Cape); Francesco Berlinghieri; Giorgio Antonio Vespucci. Elsewhere: Lisbon, reports of Dias rounding southern Africa in 1488; Indian Ocean ports, established monsoon routes.

- **Magnetic compass** [`magnetic_compass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/magnetic_compass.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. A magnetic needle and wind-rose card are familiar to Mediterranean pilots. Explanations for the needle's direction include attraction towards the celestial pole. Elsewhere: Genoa, Venice, Amalfi: compass makers.
- **Magnetic variation (declination) and deviation** [`magnetic_declination`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/magnetic_declination.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Some compass-sundials mark a local offset. Columbus records the changing bearing of the needle relative to Polaris in 1492. Pilots lack a chart of variation. Elsewhere: Nuremberg: sundial compasses marked with the offset; Flanders: 'corrected' compasses.
- **Dead reckoning (course, speed, time; log line and traverse table)** [`dead_reckoning_log_line`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/dead_reckoning_log_line.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Pilots use compass, half-hour glass, chart and the toleta de marteloio; speed is guessed by eye. The log line is unknown. Elsewhere: Venice, Genoa: pilots trained in the marteloio.
- **Latitude from Pole Star and noon Sun (quadrant, astrolabe, cross-staff, kamal)** [`latitude_astrolabe_quadrant`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/latitude_astrolabe_quadrant.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept high. Tuscan astronomers measure altitudes. Portuguese pilots use Polaris, and José Vizinho observed the noon Sun on the Guinea coast in 1485. Local: Lorenzo della Volpaia (instrument maker); Toscanelli's gnomon in the Duomo (1475); Regiomontanus' printed Ephemerides. Elsewhere: Portugal, José Vizinho's observations; Castile, Zacuto's astronomical tables composed in Salamanca; Indian Ocean, stellar altitude navigation.

- **Longitude by marine chronometer** [`longitude_chronometer`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/longitude_chronometer.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept high. Pilots estimate easting and westing by dead reckoning. Astronomers can compare eclipse times on land. Existing clocks cannot keep reference time on an ocean passage. - **Nautical charts and map projections (portolans, Ptolemy, Mercator)** [`map_projection_charts`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/map_projection_charts.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Florentine cartographers use Ptolemy's projections. Mediterranean pilots use portolan charts with rhumb lines. The two traditions solve different problems. Local: Henricus Martellus; Francesco Rosselli (engraved maps); Berlinghieri's Geographia (Florence 1482). Elsewhere: Genoa, Venice and Majorca, portolan chart makers.

- **Tides and tide tables** [`tides_tide_tables`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tides_tide_tables.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium.
